items.name: Sabunike Mol (pier beach)
items.description: The closest beach to the villa: a sandy shore next to the small Sabunike pier, about 500 m (a 6-minute walk) from the apartments. The seabed slopes very gently into clear water, so small children can paddle a long way out. Beach Bar Palma is right at the pier.
items.tips: Walk, don't drive. Rent an umbrella or bring your own, because there is very little natural shade. There can be a strip of small stones before the sand, so water shoes help toddlers. Windsurfers use the open water further out on windy afternoons.

items.name: Sabunike Naturist Beach
items.description: A designated naturist (textile-free) beach on the gravelly shore just north of Sabunike, about 850 m from the villa. It is undeveloped and quiet even in high season.
items.tips: No bar or seating on the beach, so bring water and shade. A dog-friendly stretch is reported right next to it (see unmappedCandidates).

items.name: Queen's Beach
items.description: One of Croatia's best-known sandy beaches: a long strip of sand and warm, shallow water running from Sabunike south-east towards Nin, with Velebit mountain behind it. Local legend ties the name to a Croatian queen. The healing mud of the Nin lagoon is right behind it.
items.tips: The northern (Sabunike) end is about 1.4 km from the villa on foot and quieter than the Nin end. The afternoon maestral brings windsurfers, and the Surfmania windsurf centre is on this beach, so keep small swimmers close to shore on windy days.

items.name: Nin Lagoon healing-mud beach
items.description: The shallow Nin lagoon next to Queen's Beach is the largest healing-mud (peloid) site in Croatia. Visitors cover themselves in the black mud, let it dry in the sun, then rinse it off in the warm shallows. In summer, open-air mud therapy combined with sea-water therapy is offered by the beach.
items.tips: Skip it if you have a heart condition or high blood pressure, and ask a doctor if unsure. Wear old swimwear because the mud stains. Pair it with a swim at Queen's Beach, 10-15 minutes' walk from the villa.

items.name: Škrapavac Beach
items.description: A sandy bay at Privlaka's southern end, sheltered from the bura wind. It has a small inflatable water park, a children's playground, a beach bar and clear, shallow water. The Zadar tourist board calls it 'perfect for kids and non-swimmers'.
items.tips: Pedal boats and jet skis are for rent, and a mini-market right behind the beach covers picnic supplies. Walk about 1 km south-east along the shore to Bilotinjak for wilder sand.

items.name: Ždrijac Beach
items.description: Long sandy beach on the Ždrijac spit just outside Nin's old town, counted among Croatia's top kitesurfing spots. A kite and windsurf school works from the beach, and the shallow sandy bottom suits learners and families alike.
items.tips: The car park (about 200 spaces) fills by late morning in August, so cycle from the villa if you can. Kiters and swimmers share the shore, so stay inside the marked zones. Spring and autumn bring stronger wind for experienced riders; summer maestral (about 8-12 kn) suits beginners.

items.name: Bilotinjak Beach
items.description: A wild natural bay of fine golden sand between reddish rock and a sandy dune, between Privlaka and Zaton. There is no bar, no toilets and no showers, which is why it still feels secluded in summer.
items.tips: Bring water, food and an umbrella: there is no shade and no infrastructure. The access road is narrow and rough and the small parking area fills early, so arrive before 10:00 or cycle (about 3 km from the villa as the crow flies). Travel guides mention dogs swimming here, but no official dog rule was found.

items.name: Zaton Holiday Resort Beach
items.description: The mostly sandy, partly pebbly 1.2 km beach of the large Zaton Holiday Resort, with a shallow entry, water slides, an inflatable water park, beach volleyball and pine shade. The resort describes it as pet-friendly and advertises a Blue Flag.
items.tips: OSM tags the resort beach as access=customers, so check whether day visitors are let in (or charged) before driving over. It is a good fallback for families when the wind is up at Sabunike.

items.name: Ričina Beach
items.description: A sheltered cove of fine sand and gravel with low grass on the Vrsi side of the Nin bay, looking out to Velebit and Pag. In season it has a beach bar, an inflatable water park, scooter rental and palm-leaf parasols. The sandy, shallow bottom suits families.
items.tips: Reached by a gravel road that ordinary cars can manage; parking is tight in peak season and some visitors come by boat. Walk north along the shore to get away from the crowd in front of the bar. Drive via Nin: it is only 4.5 km from the villa as the crow flies, but much further by road.

items.name: Pliša Beach
items.description: A small sandy beach south of Zaton with a seaside promenade, backed by golden sand cliffs and reeds. The water is notably clear and good for a casual snorkel. The Demos Pliša beach bar and a small marina are right next to it.
items.tips: Combine it with a walk or ride along the Zaton promenade. It works well as an evening swim and sunset stop.

items.name: Radovanjica Beach, Vir
items.description: A south-coast beach near Vir town that mixes concrete sunbathing areas and gravel with a very flat sandy sea entry. Toilets, food, sunbed rental and pedal boats are on hand.
items.tips: The concrete platforms make it easy for grandparents and buggies; the sandy shallows keep toddlers happy.

items.name: Duboka Draga
items.description: A pebble-and-rock cove on the Vrsi coast with very clear water, which visitors rate as the area's best snorkeling spot. It has a seasonal beach bar and a public toilet but is otherwise natural, with views of Velebit.
items.tips: Bring your own mask, snorkel and water shoes, because the rocks are sharp and there is no rental. The last stretch is a gravel road of about 1 km; parking is at the end of the asphalt, 10-15 minutes' walk from the cove. There is no shade, so arrive early and bring your own.

items.name: Jadro Beach, Vir
items.description: Vir's main town beach along the promenade: fine pebbles over a sandy seabed with a flat, family-friendly entry. Water sports, rentals, cafés and shops are right behind it.
items.tips: The bridge from Privlaka to Vir backs up on summer weekends, so go early or cycle across. Changing cabins are on site.

items.name: Sapavac Beach, Vir
items.description: A sheltered bay on Vir's south-west shore with mostly sand, some gravel and rock, pine shade and warm, shallow water that is especially good for families with small children.
items.tips: There is only a mobile toilet on the beach, with cafés a few minutes' walk away. The deep sand is not suitable for wheelchairs.

items.name: Pedinka Beach, Vir
items.description: A south-Vir beach of rock, gravel and concrete with flat shallows that one guide calls ideal for toddlers and non-swimmers. It has a beach bar and its own car park.
items.tips: The rocky edges are worth a look with a mask; use the flat middle section for small children.

items.name: Biskupljača & Lozice Beach, Vir
items.description: A north-west Vir beach at Lozice with gravel, small stones and patches of sand. It has a café, a restaurant, toilets, sunbed rental and water sports, and is suitable for children.
items.tips: It is quieter than Jadro. Vir's other 'Duboka Draga' cove is nearby along the north-west coast.

items.name: Ljubač Bay Beach
items.description: A long, gently sloping sandy bay at Ljubač, opening to the north-west, with a big standing area in shallow water and few boats. The afternoon thermal wind regularly reaches about 15 knots, which draws windsurfers, foilers and kiters looking for a break from crowded Nin.
items.tips: You can park right at the beach at the south-western end of the bay. Bora days are gusty with a rough cross-sea here. Look for the ruins of the medieval Ljubač fortress (Stari grad Ljubač) on the headland.

items.name: Lanterna (Vir lighthouse point)
items.description: The western tip of Vir, at a lighthouse built in 1881, largely destroyed in WWII and rebuilt in 1950. It is remote and open to the west, which makes it one of the island's best places to watch the sun go down.
items.tips: Go for the sunset rather than a beach day. There are no facilities, and the lighthouse building is now a private holiday villa, so stay on the public shore.

unmapped.name: Sabunike dog-friendly stretch (next to the FKK beach)
unmapped.why: kroati.de: 'Gleich nebenan gibt es des Weiteren auch schöne Abschnitte für Hundehalter' (right next to the naturist beach north of Sabunike). If confirmed, this would be the closest dog beach to the villa, under 1 km away.

unmapped.name: Privlaka / Vir dog beach by the Vir bridge (Kažin / Vrilo)
unmapped.why: Several sources report a dog beach near the Vir bridge: BringFido (search snippet) says a fenced dog beach over 100 m long at 'Kažin' near the Vir bridge with parking; kroati.de (Vir page) mentions a dog section near Vrilo (Privlaka) and a dog beach near the bridge on Vir's eastern edge. Beaches-Searcher lists a 'Pseća plaža' at Zarići. The anchor is the Virski most bridge (Nominatim), not the beach.

unmapped.name: Mostina Beach, Privlaka
unmapped.why: Official zadar.hr: sandy, for families with small children; showers, changing booths, eco toilet, and separate barrier-free sea access for disabled guests. placesofjuma says it is in front of Dalmacija camp near the village centre. A strong candidate for accessibility and grandparent audiences, but there is no OSM pin.

unmapped.name: Vrilo Beach, Privlaka
unmapped.why: About 330 m long and mostly sand, with some pebbly corners and concrete sunbathing areas. It has a few straw parasols, a small seasonal beach bar, parking, changing rooms and a toilet (kroati.de), and a popular dog section. kroati.de places it on Privlaka's east coast, placesofjuma on the north coast; the location is unconfirmed.

unmapped.name: Selo Beach, Privlaka
unmapped.why: Golden sand with a flat entry next to Privlaka's small fishing harbour, popular with families. Loungers, umbrellas and a restaurant terrace; no parking at the beach.

unmapped.name: Partenza Beach, Privlaka
unmapped.why: A sandy beach next to the Vir bridge on Privlaka's north-west side, with a gentle shelf suiting small children and non-swimmers, and the Partenza beach bar.

unmapped.name: Kozjak Beach, Vir
unmapped.why: Concrete, stones and sandy patches by the small settlement and cape of Kozjak, a few steps from the ruins of the Kaštelina fortress on Vir. Entry is gentle and suits children; there is no infrastructure. No OSM pin.

unmapped.name: Duboka Draga, Vir (Lozice)
unmapped.why: A second 'Duboka Draga': a quiet cove of gravel, sand and red rocks on Vir's north-west coast near Lozice, with only a beach bar. It might be the owner's intended snorkeling spot.

unmapped.name: Prodorica Beach, Nin
unmapped.why: A named OSM beach east of Nin old town (no tags beyond the name). No descriptive source was found.

unmapped.name: Petrčane public beach
unmapped.why: A pebble beach in OSM about 8.6 km straight-line south of the villa, but roughly 25 km by road. No descriptive source was found.

unmapped.name: Ričina / Dubrovnik / Perilo beaches, Povljana (Pag)
unmapped.why: Sandy beaches on Pag's southern shore, about 8-12 km straight-line across the water but a long drive by road via the Pag bridge. They include an OSM dog-designated beach (way/1559853964) and the OSM 'Ričina' beach. They are excluded from items because they are not practical half-day trips from the villa.
